_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for F retrospectives (retro/build_f.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date: a filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern). Ford's earnings 8-Ks of 2021-2026 were accepted after the close (16:07-16:14 ET) and its 10-Qs and 10-Ks the same evenings, so a print, its 10-Q or 10-K, and a Q4 print's 10-K share one date. Generated by a script from row strings of the filings (each checked with retro/tools/verbatim.py); every growth rate, margin change and rule-T value is computed. See retro/README.md, 'F'.

history_vintages.why: Ford Motor Company 'designs, manufactures, markets, and services a full line of Ford trucks, utility vehicles, and cars – increasingly including electrified versions – and Lincoln luxury vehicles'; among its risk factors, 'Industry sales volume in any of Ford’s key markets can be volatile and could decline if there is a financial crisis, recession, or significant geopolitical event,” a sustained decline in vehicle sales would have a substantial adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flow' and 'Ford’s results are dependent on sales of larger, more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States' (its own FY2020 10-K); its MD&A adds that government regulations 'and other factors that accelerate the transition to electrified vehicles, may increase the cost of vehicles by more than the perceived benefit to consumers and dampen margins' (a trend, not a risk factor naming a shift away from its combustion-engine vehicles)

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'F'): the decade of the FY2020 10-K, the vintage public on 2022-01-07, is 2011-2020. Each change comes from the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years, as a filing tabulates it (no sums, no narrative-derived levels); a measure the filings report for fewer years takes the changes they report (the AVGO rule). XBULL best, BULL median, BASE worst, BEAR one median-to-worst step beyond the worst.
